a0928b1a9e69.title: Algorithms
a0928b1a9e69.content:
Algorithms - Design and Analysis Notes

An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem. Algorithm
analysis measures time complexity and space complexity, often expressed with
Big-O notation. Common complexities include constant, logarithmic, linear,
linearithmic, quadratic, and exponential time.

Sorting algorithms include bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort, merge
sort, quick sort, and heap sort. Merge sort and quick sort use divide and
conquer with average time complexity O(n log n). Searching algorithms include
linear search and binary search. Binary search requires sorted data and runs
in logarithmic time.

Algorithm design paradigms include divide and conquer, greedy algorithms,
dynamic programming, and backtracking. Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths
in graphs. Depth first search and breadth first search traverse trees and
graphs. Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself with a base case
to terminate.

Efficient algorithms depend on appropriate data structures such as hash tables,
heaps, and balanced trees. Ranking and searching documents also relies on
algorithms for scoring and sorting results by relevance.

e55ef712e264.title: Datastructures
e55ef712e264.content:
Data Structures - Study Notes

Data structures organize and store data efficiently. Common data structures
include arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, hash tables, and
heaps. Each data structure has trade-offs in time and space complexity.

A stack follows last-in first-out order with push and pop operations. A queue
follows first-in first-out order with enqueue and dequeue operations. A linked
list consists of nodes where each node stores data and a reference to the next
node. Doubly linked lists also store a reference to the previous node.

Trees are hierarchical data structures with a root node, child nodes, and leaf
nodes. Binary trees restrict each node to at most two children. Binary search
trees maintain ordering for fast lookup. Graphs consist of vertices and edges
and can be directed or undirected. Hash tables use a hash function to map keys
to buckets, providing average constant time lookup.

Understanding data structures is essential for algorithms, database indexing,
and operating systems. Python lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries are built-in
data structures implemented with efficient algorithms.

74cd817c3420.title: Dbms
74cd817c3420.content:
Database Management Systems - DBMS Notes

A database is an organized collection of data. A database management system (DBMS)
is software that manages databases and provides an interface for users and
applications. Examples include MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite.

Database normalization is a process that reduces redundancy and improves data
consistency by organizing tables. Normalization involves dividing large tables
into smaller tables and defining relationships between them. The normal forms
include first normal form, second normal form, and third normal form. Database
normalization reduces redundancy and improves data consistency by organizing
tables with primary keys and foreign keys.

Structured Query Language (SQL) is used to query and manipulate databases.
Common SQL commands include SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TABLE, and
JOIN operations. An index in a database speeds up retrieval. Transactions ensure
ACID properties: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

The entity relationship model describes entities, attributes, and relationships.
Primary keys uniquely identify rows, while foreign keys link tables together.
Concurrency control and deadlock handling are important in multi-user database
systems. Database indexing, query optimization, and schema design affect
performance of database normalization and retrieval.

b6bad5a68eba.title: Networks
b6bad5a68eba.content:
Computer Networks - Networking Notes

A computer network connects devices to share data. The OSI model has seven
layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, and
application. The TCP/IP model simplifies this into four layers. IP addressing
and routing move packets across networks.

TCP is a reliable connection-oriented transport protocol with acknowledgments
and retransmission. UDP is a faster connectionless protocol used for streaming.
HTTP and HTTPS operate at the application layer for the web. DNS resolves
domain names to IP addresses. DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.

Network devices include hubs, switches, routers, and firewalls. Ethernet and
WiFi are common link technologies. Congestion control, flow control, and error
detection improve reliability. Socket programming in Python allows building
client server applications over TCP and UDP. Network security uses encryption,
authentication, and firewalls to protect data.

5f99a34fc81e.title: Os
5f99a34fc81e.content:
Operating Systems - OS Notes

An operating system manages hardware and software resources. It acts as an
intermediary between users and hardware. Core functions include process
management, memory management, file system management, and device management.

A process is a program in execution. Process scheduling algorithms include first
come first served, shortest job first, round robin, and priority scheduling.
Inter-process communication uses pipes, message queues, and shared memory.
Threads share memory within a process and enable concurrent execution.

Deadlock occurs when processes wait for resources held by each other. Deadlock
detection and deadlock prevention are essential. The four Coffman conditions
for deadlock are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular
wait. Deadlock detection algorithms examine resource allocation graphs.
Banker's algorithm avoids deadlock by safe state checks.

Memory management uses paging, segmentation, and virtual memory. The file system
organizes files in directories. Synchronization problems include the critical
section, semaphores, monitors, and the readers writers problem. Popular
operating systems include Linux, Windows, and macOS.

5dd1fab4f415.title: Python
5dd1fab4f415.content:
Python Programming Language - Introduction Notes

Python is a high-level programming language known for its simplicity and readability.
It was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Python supports
multiple programming paradigms including procedural programming, object oriented
programming, and functional programming.

Python is an interpreted language, which means code is executed line by line by
the Python interpreter. It has dynamic typing, automatic memory management, and
a large standard library. Common data structures in Python include lists, tuples,
sets, and dictionaries. Lists are mutable ordered sequences, tuples are immutable
ordered sequences, sets store unique unordered elements, and dictionaries store
key value pairs.

Functions in Python are defined with the def keyword. Lambda functions provide a
way to create small anonymous functions. List comprehensions offer a concise way
to create lists. Iterators and generators allow efficient iteration over sequences,
with generators using the yield keyword to produce values lazily.

Exception handling in Python uses try, except, finally blocks. File handling is
done with the open function, supporting read, write, and append modes. Modules
and packages help organize code, and object oriented programming is supported
through classes, inheritance, and polymorphism.

Python is widely used in web development with frameworks like Django, in data
analysis, automation, and scripting. The Django web framework follows the model
template view pattern and provides an object relational mapper for database access.

fac79b61bb0e.title: Software Engineering
fac79b61bb0e.content:
Software Engineering - SE Notes

Software engineering applies systematic methods to build reliable software.
The software development life cycle includes requirement analysis, design,
implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Common process models
include waterfall, iterative, spiral, and agile methodologies.

Agile follows iterative sprints with a product backlog, sprint backlog, user
stories, story points, daily standups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives. Scrum
defines roles such as product owner, scrum master, and development team. A
Kanban board tracks work in columns like backlog, todo, in progress, code
review, testing, and done. A burndown chart tracks remaining story points over
sprint duration.

Version control with Git and GitHub enables collaboration. Branches, commits,
pull requests, and code reviews maintain quality. Continuous integration with
GitHub Actions runs automated tests on push and pull request. Testing includes
unit tests, integration tests, and system tests using frameworks like unittest.

Design principles include modularity, separation of concerns, and documentation.
Requirements, architecture diagrams, and definitions of done guide development.

b74912f4f80b.title: Sql
b74912f4f80b.content:
SQL and Database Programming Notes

SQL is the standard language for relational databases such as MySQL. A table
stores rows and columns. The SELECT statement retrieves data, WHERE filters
rows, ORDER BY sorts results, GROUP BY aggregates, and JOIN combines tables.

Database indexes improve query speed. A primary key uniquely identifies each
row. Normalization organizes schema to avoid duplication. Transactions group
statements so they succeed or fail together.

Python programs connect to MySQL with a database driver, execute SQL queries,
fetch results, and handle database errors with exception handling. Django
models map Python classes to database tables. Understanding SQL complements
database normalization theory covered in DBMS notes.
